sourceType: Official Rajasthan Tourism website (Government of Rajasthan)
note: Facts extracted below; prose summaries in our own words, not copied verbatim from the source.
about: One of Rajasthan's oldest cities, with traditions traced to Viratnagar flourishing around 1500 BC. Also known as Matasya Desh, where the Pandavas spent their 13-year exile. Nestled in the Aravalli range's green hills, home to beautiful palaces and forts. Dense forest cover hosts Bengal tigers, golden jackals, grey partridges, and white-throated kingfishers. Gateway City of Rajasthan.

places.name: Bala Qila (Young Fort)
places.facts: Built on 10th-century mud fort foundations; strong fortifications, graceful marble columns, delicate latticed balconies; six gates; accessible by road through Pratap Bandh forest; buffer forest safari available.

places.name: Alwar City Palace
places.facts: Built 1793 by Raja Bakhtawar Singh; mélange of Rajputana and Islamic styles; graceful marble pavilions on lotus-flower bases; now District Collectorate.

places.name: Government Museum
places.facts: Rare manuscripts, Ragamala paintings, miniatures, extensive armory displays; window timing 9:45am-4:45pm.

places.name: Sariska Tiger Reserve
places.facts: First tiger reserve to successfully relocate tigers; declared sanctuary 1955, National Park 1979; forest closed Wednesdays.

places.name: Siliserh Lake
places.facts: Tranquil lake with hunting palace built 1845; now RTDC hotel; boating available; winter water birds and crocodiles.

howToReach.rail: Connected to Jaipur, Delhi, and other major cities
howToReach.road: 160 km from Delhi, 150 km from Jaipur
